svg.title: The container you pick chooses the exponent
svg.desc: A row of list cells scanned one at a time for a linear membership test, beside a set drawn as eight hash slots where one hash jump lands directly on the answer, with 367867x written between them. Below, list.insert(0) shuffles every element right at 311 microseconds while deque.appendleft writes one pointer in 16 nanoseconds. At the bottom a generator pipeline carries one record at a time and peaks at 14.3 MB, against a list holding all 12.2 million records at 10 499 MB, crossed out in red.
svg.text: The container you pick chooses the exponent
one box at a time, every time
every element shuffles right: 311 319 ns at 1M
the same 2 GB file, two shapes
one record in flight -> peak 14.3 MB
the most common accidental O(n^2) in Python
the generator never held more than one
record. That is the whole trick.
...and what happens on a hash collision?
